name: The organization

sittings.title: Sitting 1
sittings.note: The pain, in your words. Stop at the end of Part 5 if you need to — the link brings you back.

sittings.title: Sitting 2
sittings.note: Systems, people, constraints, and numbers. This is the half that most intake forms skip.

masthead.lede: This is the longer version, because at your size the answer is rarely just the pain — it’s the systems around it, who owns them, and what the {org} requires before anything new runs. Two sittings of about thirty minutes. Do the first one and stop; the link brings you back.
howto: Sitting 1 is the pain, in your words. The same questions I ask an owner-operator, because corporate teams tend to describe the solution they’ve already decided on. I need the problem underneath it.
Sitting 2 is the organization. Systems and exports, the people who decide and the people who’ll push back, constraints, metrics with a baseline, and what you can send me.
Nothing is graded. A half-answer beats a blank. Questions marked optional can be skipped.
Answers save in this browser as you type. They stay on this device; if you switch machines, finish on the one you started on.
rules: One occasion, not a pattern. A specific day and a number, wherever you can.
In Parts 2–4, don’t use the words app, software, system, automate, dashboard, or AI. Write down what happened instead.
Don’t paste anything you’d need an NDA for. If your {org} requires one before sitting 2, say so in Part 10 and one comes back the same day.
masthead.after: When you submit, {consultantFirst} reads everything within two business days and sends you one page: what he heard, and the two or three things worth building first, with what each would take.

finishText: Nothing has been sent yet — your answers are only in this browser. The button below turns them into a plain text summary you can copy into an email to {consultantFirst} ({consultantEmail}), download as a file, or print. Attachments go by email to the same address.
